title: `output_format='python'` and `'php'` produce broken string literals when the SQL contains backslashes
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

The python and php output formats are supposed to give a string literal that evaluates back to the SQL, but backslashes in the SQL are copied as is, so a backslash before a quote ends the generated string early.

```python
import sqlparse
sql = "select '\\foo\\'"   # the SQL text is: select '\foo\'
print(sqlparse.format(sql, output_format='python'))
print(sqlparse.format(sql, output_format='php'))
```
Expected:
```
sql = 'select \'\\foo\\\''
$sql = "select '\\foo\\'";
```
Actual:
```
sql = 'select \'\foo\\''
$sql = "select '\foo\'";
```
The python line is not even valid Python, and in PHP `\'` and `\f` change meaning.

Every backslash in the SQL must be escaped in the generated literal (as well as the quote character), so the output always evaluates to exactly the original SQL.
acceptance: The reported SQL produces the expected python and php output
Generated python and php literals evaluate back to the original SQL for input with backslashes and quotes
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
